issues.t: Four-speed automatic slipping or failing
issues.sym: The engine revs without the van speeding up, shifts are delayed or harsh, the van gets stuck in one gear, or it won't move at all.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in these vans wears its clutches and torque converter. Owners report failures from about 30,000 miles up, sometimes more than once, and low or old fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the fluid level with the engine warm and use only the correct Chrysler-spec fluid. If it slips or gets stuck in a gear, drive gently to a transmission shop for diagnosis before the damage spreads.

issues.t: Airbag light on from a failing clockspring or sensor
issues.sym: The airbag warning light flashes or stays on. The horn may also stop working, and some owners report dash lights or turn signals acting up at the same time.
issues.why: The clockspring, a coiled ribbon cable behind the steering wheel, wears and breaks the circuit to the driver airbag and horn. Faulty airbag sensors or seat belt parts can also trigger the light. Airbag complaints are the most common category for these years.
issues.next: Treat the airbag light as a sign the airbags may not deploy. Have a shop read the airbag codes soon. Never take apart the steering wheel yourself.

issues.t: Rusted brake lines leak and cause sudden brake loss
issues.sym: The brake pedal sinks toward the floor, braking suddenly gets weak, or brake fluid is found leaking under the van.
issues.why: Steel brake lines under the van rust, especially in road-salt areas, until they leak or burst. Owners report losing brakes while driving.
issues.next: If the pedal goes soft or low, stop driving and have the van towed. Ask a shop to inspect all brake lines for rust and replace any corroded sections.

issues.t: Engine stalls while driving
issues.sym: The engine dies suddenly, sometimes after running for a while, and may be hard to restart. Power steering and brake assist get heavy when it stalls.
issues.why: Owners report stalling that parts swaps such as the engine computer or fuel filter didn't cure; a failing fuel pump is a common suspect. The cause varies from van to van.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer firmly to a safe spot and press the brake hard. Have a shop check fuel pressure and scan for codes while the problem is happening.

issues.t: Headlights cut out briefly while driving
issues.sym: The headlights shut off for a moment and come back on while driving at night.
issues.why: Owners trace it to the electrical control module or headlight circuit; dealers sometimes can't reproduce it.
issues.next: If the lights go out, slow down and get off the road safely. Have the headlight switch, wiring and module checked.

issues.t: Instrument panel gauges or lights stop working
issues.sym: The speedometer, gauges or instrument panel lighting stop working, sometimes on and off.
issues.why: The instrument cluster fails internally or loses its connection, and a worn clockspring can also take out some dash functions.
issues.next: Don't rely on a dead speedometer. A shop can test the cluster; a rebuilt cluster is often an option instead of a new one.

issues.t: Air conditioning blows warm or compressor fails
issues.sym: The A/C blows only warm air, sometimes after a squealing noise from the engine bay.
issues.why: The A/C compressor wears out or seizes; a refrigerant leak can also leave the system empty.
issues.next: Have the system pressure-tested before adding refrigerant. If the compressor squeals or seizes, turn the A/C off and get it checked so the belt isn't damaged.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaks, a burning smell or smoke from under the hood, or the steering gets heavy. Some owners report a hose blowing off.
issues.why: A power steering hose could leak fluid onto hot engine parts and cause an under-hood fire. Chrysler recalled about 681,000 minivans to fix it.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, pull over, shut off the engine and get out. Ask a Chrysler dealer to check by VIN that recall 04V386 was done; it is free.

issues.t: Oil leak from the oil filter adapter
issues.sym: Oil drips under the front of the van or coats the area around the oil filter, usually at high mileage.
issues.why: The seal on the oil filter adapter, which the filter screws onto, wears out and leaks. Chrysler released a revised adapter.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and top up. Have the adapter seal or adapter replaced before the oil runs low.

issues.t: Front clunk or rattle from sway bar links and bushings
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the front over bumps or rough roads.
issues.why: The front sway bar end links and bushings wear out, usually around 60,000 to 130,000 miles.
issues.next: Not urgent, but have the front end inspected to confirm the source, since worn ball joints can make similar noises and are more serious.

issues.t: Fuel rail leak with gas smell in the cabin
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell inside or around the van, sometimes with fuel wetness on top of the engine.
issues.why: An owner of a 2.4L van reports the fuel rail leaking gasoline near the engine.
issues.next: A gas smell is a fire risk. Don't drive it; have it towed and inspected, and don't smoke or use flames nearby.

issues.t: Front lower control arm bolt can break (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. If the bolt breaks, the control arm can separate and you could lose control.
issues.why: A bolt holding the front lower control arm to the crossmember could fracture. Chrysler recalled the vans to fix it.
issues.next: Ask a Chrysler dealer to confirm recall 01V152 was completed on your VIN. It is free.

issues.t: Radio short circuit can start a speaker fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from a speaker or the radio.
issues.why: A short circuit in the factory radio could overheat a speaker and start a fire.
issues.next: If you smell burning from the speakers, turn the radio off and stop the van. Ask a dealer to confirm recall 04V531 is done.

issues.t: Sliding door lock linkage can let the door partly open (recall)
issues.sym: The sliding door may not stay fully latched and could partly open.
issues.why: A problem with the sliding door lock linkage could let the door open part of the way.
issues.next: Use the child locks and make sure the door is fully shut before driving. Ask a dealer to check that the recall repair was done.

issues.t: Child seat attachment information missing (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The child seat anchor parts or owner's manual instructions may be wrong.
issues.why: A child seat might not be attached properly in a crash, which raises the risk of injury to the child.
issues.next: Ask a Chrysler dealer to confirm recall 01V310 was done, and follow the corrected child seat instructions.

issues.t: Some replacement brake master cylinders can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal and longer stopping distances. Applies only if the master cylinder was replaced with certain aftermarket parts.
issues.why: Some aftermarket replacement master cylinders could leak brake fluid and lower brake pressure.
issues.next: If the pedal feels soft, stop driving and have it inspected. If the master cylinder has been replaced, ask the shop which brand was used.

issues.t: Some replacement fuel filters can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel dripping under the van. Applies only if the fuel filter was replaced with certain aftermarket filters.
issues.why: Two aftermarket fuel filter makers recalled filters that could leak fuel, which could stall the engine or start a fire.
issues.next: If you smell gas, don't drive the van. If the fuel filter has been replaced, have a shop check the brand and look for leaks.

issues.t: Harsh shifts or jerks from the nine-speed automatic
issues.sym: Rough or jarring shifts, a bang when shifting into Drive or Reverse, or a jerk between gears. Some owners of the same van as a Pacifica report slipping or a Service Transmission message.
issues.why: The nine-speed automatic shared with the Pacifica is known for rough shift quality. Dealers often call it normal, but some vans need software updates or internal repairs such as a valve body.
issues.next: Note when it happens and ask a dealer to check for software updates and stored codes. If it slips or shows a transmission warning, get it checked right away while under warranty.

issues.t: Ticking engine from worn rocker arms
issues.sym: A ticking from the top of the engine, sometimes with a misfire code and the check engine light.
issues.why: Rocker arms (cam followers) in the 3.6L Pentastar V6 can wear or fail. Chrysler revised the part, but newer engines still show the problem.
issues.next: Have a ticking engine checked soon. If a misfire code is present, avoid hard driving. The repair is mostly labor and is worth doing before a camshaft gets damaged.

issues.t: Oil or coolant leak from the oil filter housing
issues.sym: Oil or coolant pooling in the valley on top of the engine, a burning smell, or slowly dropping oil or coolant levels.
issues.why: The plastic oil filter housing between the cylinder banks, which also holds the oil cooler, can warp or its seals can leak. Because it sits on top of the engine, the leak often isn't seen until it is large.
issues.next: Look at the top of the engine with a flashlight at each oil change. If you see oil or coolant there, get it fixed promptly; low coolant can overheat the engine.

issues.t: Ticking behind the dash from the recirculation door actuator
issues.sym: A ticking or clicking from behind the front A/C vents, often after the van is turned off.
issues.why: The small motor that moves the recirculation air door fails. An owner found the same noise on several other 2020-2023 Voyagers and Pacificas.
issues.next: It is not a safety problem. A dealer can replace the actuator; check if your warranty still covers it.

issues.t: Clunk when lifting off the gas at low speed
issues.sym: A clunk or thump from the front when you let off the accelerator in a low gear.
issues.why: In one reported case the dealer found a loose front axle nut and tightened it.
issues.next: Have the axle nuts, engine mounts and suspension checked. A loose axle nut can damage the wheel bearing if ignored.

issues.t: Stop/start unavailable or battery charging warnings
issues.sym: Messages saying the auto stop/start needs service or is unavailable, or a battery charging warning that won't clear. One owner also felt hesitation while driving.
issues.why: These vans use an auxiliary battery to support stop/start. A weak battery or charging fault sets these warnings.
issues.next: Have both batteries and the charging system tested. If a charging warning stays on, get it checked before the van leaves you stranded.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag connector may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. The side curtain airbags might not deploy in a crash.
issues.why: A connector for the side curtain airbags may not have been secured during assembly. The recall covered a small number of vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a dealer for recall 24V793. The fix is free.

issues.t: Second-row seat latch can stick open (recall)
issues.sym: A second-row seat may not lock to the floor even though it looks in place.
issues.why: A floor latch can jam open, so the seat isn't secured in a crash.
issues.next: Pull on the seat to make sure it is locked. Ask a dealer to check recall 22V181 by VIN; the repair is free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not display (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera screen stays blank when you shift into Reverse.
issues.why: A radio software fault can stop the rearview camera image from appearing.
issues.next: Back up carefully using mirrors and a look over your shoulder. A free software update fixes it (recall 24V436), at a dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Windshield wipers may not work properly (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers may not work correctly in some conditions, cutting visibility in rain or snow.
issues.why: A small number of vans were recalled for wipers that might not function properly.
issues.next: If the wipers fail in bad weather, pull over safely. Ask a dealer to check recall 22V619 by VIN.

issues.t: Steering column module weld can stop the driver airbag (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. The driver's airbag might not deploy in a crash.
issues.why: A steering column control module may not have been welded properly, which can keep the driver airbag from deploying.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check recall 24V199 by VIN. They inspect and replace the module free if needed.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may not hold pressure (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. The side curtain airbags may lose pressure too quickly in a rollover or side crash.
issues.why: Seams in the side curtain airbags may not be sealed properly, so they don't meet the federal ejection-protection standard. Recall 26V189 expands and replaces earlier recalls 25V302 and 25V573, and vans fixed under those need the new repair.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. Dealers replace the curtain airbags free; owner letters were scheduled for May 2026.

issues.t: Brake pedal sensor can disable stability control (recall)
issues.sym: Stability control warning lights may come on, and electronic stability control may stop working.
issues.why: A capacitor in the brake pedal position sensor can crack, which can switch off electronic stability control.
issues.next: Drive gently, especially on wet or icy roads, until it is fixed. Dealers inspect and replace the sensor free under recall 26V561; owner letters were scheduled for late September 2026.
